test_title: SSC Stenographer 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Ravi said that he might go to the mall.

options.text: Ravi said, "I can go to the mall".
Ravi said, "I could go to the mall."
Ravi said, "I will go to the mall."
Ravi said, "I may go to the mall".

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** Ravi said that he might go to the mall.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"might" becomes "may"**
 
 
• The modal verb "might" in indirect speech is converted to "may" in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun "he" becomes "I"**
 
 
• Pronoun "he" is changed to "I" to match direct speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "I" and ends with a period ".".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, starting with a lowercase letter after the comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I may go to the mall," said Ravi.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "I can go to the mall," said Ravi.

 
 
• The modal verb "can" changes the meaning to a statement of ability rather than possibility.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "I could go to the mall," said Ravi.
 
 
• The modal verb "could" implies a conditional or past possibility, which alters the original meaning.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "I will go to the mall," said Ravi.
 
 
• The modal verb "will" implies certainty rather than possibility, changing the original context.
